# `nish/net/tls/record-client`

A TLS 1.3 client over a byte stream: the record layer of `nish/net/tls/record` wrapped around `nish/net/tls/client`'s `TlsClient`, sans-IO. Bytes the server sent go in, bytes to send come out, and once the handshake is done application data flows both ways. The mirror of `nish/net/tls/record-server`.

```ts
import {
  TLS_RECORD_AUTH,
  TlsRecordClient,
} from "nish/net/tls/record-client";
```

```ts
const conn = new TlsRecordClient(new TlsClient(config, random, x25519Key, p256Key));
// send conn.output[conn.outputStart .. conn.outputEnd), then conn.consume(sent)
conn.receive(bytes, 0, n);                 // what the socket read
if ((conn.interest() & TLS_RECORD_AUTH) !== 0) {
  // check conn.tls.peerCertificates() and the CertificateVerify
  conn.authenticate(verified);
}
const got: i32 = conn.read(buf, 0, buf.length);   // application data
```

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="TlsRecordClient" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#tlsrecordclient">

One TLS 1.3 client connection over a stream.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

<scalar-detail title="What it adds to `TlsClient`">

Records around the handshake messages:
the ClientHello in the clear, then the client's Finished under the
handshake keys, and every key installed at the record boundary RFC 8446
§5.1 puts it on. The middlebox-compatibility `change_cipher_spec` of §D.4,
which a client that sends a session id (this one always does) owes: one,
in the clear, before its second ClientHello after a HelloRetryRequest, or
else before its first protected record; the server's is dropped from its
first handshake record until its Finished. Alerts (§6) both ways, as the
server has them: `close_notify` ends the server's stream, `user_canceled`
is passed over, any other alert ends the connection, and a refusal of this
module's or of `TlsClient`'s is sent as a fatal alert under whatever keys
the client writes with. KeyUpdate (§4.6.3) both ways, with the server's
limits: `TLS_RECORD_IDLE_LIMIT` records in a row that carry nothing, and
`TLS_RECORD_MAX_KEY_UPDATES` KeyUpdates. A NewSessionTicket is handed to
`TlsClient`, which checks and drops it; any other post-handshake message is
`unexpected_message` (no client certificate is offered, so no
CertificateRequest). A stream that ends without `close_notify` is
truncation.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Authentication is the caller's">

At `TlsClient`'s `WAIT_AUTH` the
records after the server's CertificateVerify stay in the reader and
`interest` says `TLS_RECORD_AUTH`: nothing more is read until the caller
has checked the chain and the signature and called `authenticate(true)` —
or `authenticate(false)` / `reject(alert)`, which fail the connection with
the alert sent. Nothing here proves who the server is.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Buffers">

One connection, one object: `output`, `plain` and `scratch`
are allocated with it, and `wipe` zeroes the two that hold plaintext. The
handshake's messages are sealed straight out of `TlsClient`'s own buffers.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Secrets">

As in `TlsRecordServer`: `TlsClient` holds the handshake's
secrets, this object the two application traffic secrets, one readonly
field per direction and hash length, with `readHash` and `writeHash` saying
which of each pair is live. A secret is copied out of `TlsClient` as it is
installed and the client's copy zeroed; the handshake secrets are zeroed
once the Finished messages no longer need them; a KeyUpdate overwrites
the live field in place. A failure of any kind wipes everything both
objects hold once the last alert is sealed; the client's `close_notify`,
once sealed, wipes the write direction, and the server's the read
direction; `wipe` wipes the rest (TLS-1, TLS-3 and "The client" in
`docs/security/tls.md`).

</scalar-detail>

Refusals are alerts, never panics. Written from RFC 8446 §4.6.3, §5, §6
and §D.4, not ported from another implementation.

## TlsRecordClient

One TLS 1.3 client connection over a stream. Make one per connection
around a fresh `TlsClient`, which it starts, and drive it with `receive`,
`consume`, `read`, `write` and `authenticate` as `interest` says.

The fields are readable: `state`, `alert` (the alert this client sent, or
0), `peerAlert` (the error alert the server sent, or -1), `peerClosed`
(the server's `close_notify` arrived), `tls` (the handshake: suite, ALPN,
the server's certificates, exporter secret), and the two protections with
their sequence numbers. `padding` is how many zero bytes each protected
record the client writes carries after its content type (§5.4).

```ts
class TlsRecordClient
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new TlsRecordClient(tls: TlsClient)` | Wraps `tls`, which should be fresh, and starts it: the ClientHello is sealed into `output` at once. A `tls` that has already failed, or whose ClientHello cannot be written, fails this connection with its alert queued in the clear. |
| `alert: i32` | The alert this client sent, or 0. |
| `keyUpdates: i32` | How many KeyUpdates from the server this client has taken, up to `TLS_RECORD_MAX_KEY_UPDATES`. |
| `output: u8[]` | Bytes to send are `output[outputStart .. outputEnd)`. |
| `outputEnd: i32` | Where the bytes still to send end in `output`. |
| `outputStart: i32` | Where the bytes still to send begin in `output`. |
| `padding: i32` | How many zero bytes each protected record the client writes carries after its content type (§5.4). |
| `peerAlert: i32` | The error alert the server sent, or -1 when it sent none. |
| `peerClosed: boolean` | True once the server's `close_notify` has arrived. |
| `readProtection: TlsRecordProtection` | Opens the server's records; its sequence number counts the records read at the current keys. |
| `state: i32` | Where the connection stands: one of the `TLS_RECORD_STATE_*` constants. |
| `tls: TlsClient` | The handshake underneath: read it for the suite, ALPN, the server's certificates and the exporter secret. |
| `writeProtection: TlsRecordProtection` | Seals the client's records; its sequence number counts the records written at the current keys. |
| `abort(): void` | The socket failed under the connection: it ends with nothing more sent, and every key it holds wiped. |
| `authenticate(ok: boolean): i32` | The caller's verdict on the server's certificate chain and CertificateVerify, while `interest` says `TLS_RECORD_AUTH` (`TlsClient.authenticate`): `true` reads on to the server's Finished and seals the client's; `false` fails the connection with `bad_certificate` sent. Answers 0, or a non-zero alert once the connection has failed (`failure`) — a verdict given before one is due answers `internal_error`. |
| `close(): void` | Closes the client's side (§6.1): a `close_notify`, after which `write` answers `TLS_RECORD_PIPE`. Application data already written stays ahead of the alert; the write keys are wiped once it is sealed. Closed before the handshake is done — before the client's Finished is sealed — the client reads nothing more, and the read keys and everything `TlsClient` holds are wiped at once. Nothing happens once the connection has failed or closed. |
| `consume(n: i32): void` | Lets the first `n` bytes of `output` go, once the socket has taken them, and seals what was waiting for the room. |
| `end(): void` | The server's TCP stream ended: the orderly end after its `close_notify`, truncation before it. |
| `failure(): i32` | Why a failed connection failed, never 0: the alert the client sent, else the server's error alert, else `internal_error` for a failure with no alert of its own (truncation, `abort`, `close_notify` mid-handshake). |
| `interest(): i32` | What the connection wants next, as `TLS_RECORD_*` bits: read the socket, write it, `read`, the caller's verdict on the server (`TLS_RECORD_AUTH`), or nothing more ever (`TLS_RECORD_DONE`). |
| `keyUpdate(requestPeer: boolean): i32` | Sends a KeyUpdate now, asking the server to update too when `requestPeer` (§4.6.3). Answers 0, `TLS_RECORD_AGAIN` while the handshake is under way or `output` is full, `TLS_RECORD_PIPE` once the client has closed or the connection failed, or `TLS_RECORD_RESET` when the next keys do not install. |
| `read(buf: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): i32` | Application data from the server, into `buf[off .. off + len)`: the count; 0 at the end of its stream (its `close_notify`) or for a `len` of 0; `TLS_RECORD_AGAIN` when nothing is waiting; `TLS_RECORD_RESET` once the connection has failed; `TLS_RECORD_INVALID` for a window outside `buf`. |
| `receive(data: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): i32` | Takes bytes of the server's stream, `data[off .. off + len)`, and handles every record they complete. Answers how many it took, fewer than `len` only when its buffers are full, or `TLS_RECORD_INVALID` for a window outside `data`. Once the connection has failed, the server has sent `close_notify`, or the client closed before the handshake was done, bytes are taken and dropped (§6.1). |
| `reject(alert: i32): i32` | Refuses the server with the caller's `alert` (`TlsClient.reject`), sent; answers the alert. |
| `space(): i32` | How many bytes `receive` would take now: what the socket should read at most. |
| `wipe(): void` | Wipes everything this connection holds: both traffic secrets at both hash lengths, both directions' keys, the plaintext buffers and everything `TlsClient` holds, so `read` has nothing more to give. Call it when the connection is done with. |
| `write(data: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): i32` | Application data for the server, `data[off .. off + len)`: seals as much as fits, in records of at most 2^14 bytes, and answers how much that was. A KeyUpdate goes first when the key has protected `recordLimit` records, or the server asked for one. `TLS_RECORD_AGAIN` while the handshake is under way or nothing fits, `TLS_RECORD_PIPE` once the client has closed or the connection failed, `TLS_RECORD_INVALID` for a window outside `data`. |

## Constants

<scalar-card title="64" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_RECORD_AUTH: i32`

An `interest` bit beside `nish/net/tls/record-server`'s `TLS_RECORD_*`:
the server's chain and CertificateVerify wait for the caller's verdict,
`authenticate` or `reject`.
